facts.quote: Tardigrades were first described by the German zoologist Johann August Ephraim Goeze in 1773, who called them Kleiner Wasserbär 'little water bear'.

facts.claim: Tardigrades can survive exposure to space.
facts.quote: In 2007, samples of 30 tardigrades and 30 eggs, all dehydrated, were taken on the FOTON-M3 mission and exposed to vacuum, to both vacuum and UVA & B light, or to both vacuum and the full range of solar ultraviolet, for 10 days.

facts.claim: Tardigrades can endure extreme temperatures, dehydration, and vacuum.
facts.quote: Tardigrades are capable of suspending their metabolism, going into a state of cryptobiosis. Terrestrial and freshwater tardigrades are able to tolerate long periods when water is not available, such as when the moss or pond they are living in dries out, by drawing their legs in and forming a desiccated cyst, the cryptobiotic 'tun' state, where no metabolic activity takes place.
